title: mnemonica .tactica definitions
description: Per-type declaration metadata of one .tactica source (format version 1.0/1.1). Keys are fullPaths and must match hierarchy.json node fullPaths exactly; see tactica/README.md for the join rules.

version.description: Format version. Absent means 1.0 (pre-versioning and 1.0 outputs are identical in shape).

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of generation. Informational only; readers must not require it.

definitions.description: Map from fullPath to declaration info. May be empty when the source declares no types.

name.description: The declared type name. Never collection-prefixed; equal to the last dotted segment of the entry key.

location.description: `file:line:col`, 1-based line and column, relative to the project root (forward slashes). Files outside the project root may stay absolute.

kind.description: How the type was declared. Generators write "define" (define()/lazy()) or "decorate" (@decorate()/Type.decorate()).

parent.description: The parent type's fullPath, null at a root. Must match another key in this file (and a hierarchy.json node) when non-null.

strictChain.description: Whether the type chain enforces strict chaining semantics.

blockErrors.description: Whether errors thrown during construction are blocked (swallowed into the chain).

fields.description: The type's own fields in declaration order — own meaning declared ahead of time by the type's definition (this annotation, class body or constructor assignments), not its runtime instance layer; a field the parent also declares is listed again. Optional: absent means the generator did not record them (a TypeScript reader may fall back to .tactica/types.ts); an empty array means the type has none.

args.description: The constructor's parameters in declaration order — what it consumes to produce its fields. The receiver (`this`, the parent instance) is not listed: `parent` names its type. Optional: absent means the generator did not record them; an empty array means the constructor takes none.

name.description: The field name as declared in the source language.

type.description: The field's type as source-language text (e.g. `string`, `[]int`, `list[str] | None`). Display only; readers never parse it.

optional.description: Whether the field may be absent (TS `?`, a Python default/None, a Go pointer or omitempty — each generator documents its rule).

name.description: The parameter name as declared in the source language.

type.description: The parameter's type as source-language text; for a rest parameter, the type as the language writes it. Display only; readers never parse it.

optional.description: Whether the caller may omit the argument (TS `?` or a default value, a Python default — each generator documents its rule). Absent means false. A rest parameter carries no `optional`: it may always receive nothing.

kind.description: How the parameter receives its value. Absent means an ordinary parameter. Generators write "rest" (the trailing positional rest: TS `...xs`, Go `xs ...T`, Python `*args`, Java `T... xs`), "keywordRest" (Python `**kwargs`: the leftover arguments passed by name), "keywordOnly" (a Python parameter after `*`, passed only by name) or "positionalOnly" (a Python parameter before `/`, passed only by position). An open string: readers tolerate values they do not know rather than failing.
